EDRD 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
EDRD 399.subject: EDRD
EDRD 399.title: Independent Study

EDRD 430.description: Examination and implementation of the key concepts, content, goals, and strategies in teaching reading and the language arts in the elementary school. Students will work with elementary children in a school setting to learn literacy concepts and instructional strategies. Admission to the B.A. program in elementary education, children’s literature course. Designated for undergraduate students seeking initial certification.
EDRD 430.subject: EDRD
EDRD 430.title: Elementary Literacy Instruction I

EDRD 431.description: Seminar and supervised one-on-one field experience focused on reading assessment of and instruction for individual children and groups of children. Restricted to: Undergraduate students pursuing teacher certification.
EDRD 431.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: admission to the professional program.
EDRD 431.subject: EDRD
EDRD 431.title: Reading Assessment

EDRD 500.description: A survey of research and practice which facilitates students' literacy skills in the content areas. For K-12 content area teachers of art, dance, physical education, foreign language, music and theatre.
EDRD 500.subject: EDRD
EDRD 500.title: Content Area Literacy PK-12

EDRD 511.description: Diagnostic and prescriptive modes of teaching reading to adults, based on the physical, psychological, intellectual, and social characteristics of the adult learner.
EDRD 511.subject: EDRD
EDRD 511.title: Teaching Reading to Adults I

EDRD 512.description: Preparation of materials for teaching basic reading skills to adults and practicum experiences in teaching adults to read.
EDRD 512.subject: EDRD
EDRD 512.title: Teaching Reading to Adults II

EDRD 514.description: Study of the various phases of reading in their relation to a modern program of education and the place of reading in the curriculum. Emphasis on modern practices in the classroom teaching of reading.
EDRD 514.subject: EDRD
EDRD 514.title: Teaching of Reading in the Elementary School

EDRD 518.description: The place of reading instruction in high schools, the programming of special services in reading instruction, methods of teaching basic and developmental reading skills, and case studies of programs. Demonstrations of tests and devices.
EDRD 518.subject: EDRD
EDRD 518.title: Reading in the Secondary School

EDRD 600.description: An overview of reading and its curriculum implications: grades K-12 and adults. Emphasis is placed on current trends and issues and related methodologies.
EDRD 600.subject: EDRD
EDRD 600.title: Foundations of Reading Instruction

EDRD 650.description: Integrating appropriate literature into traditional and alternative reading programs. Identifying appropriate literature for classroom use and recreational reading. Use of literature as a means of developing and reinforcing reading skills.
EDRD 650.subject: EDRD
EDRD 650.title: Teaching Reading Through A Literature Emphasis

EDRD 651.description: A survey of analysis of electronic and non-print media themes and messages aimed at youth, with special emphasis on design and implementation of curricula for enhancing children’s media literacy.
EDRD 651.subject: EDRD
EDRD 651.title: Introduction to Teaching Media Literacy

EDRD 700.description: An active and reflective experience of process writing within multiple genres and multimodal literacies with classroom applications.
EDRD 700.subject: EDRD
EDRD 700.title: Multimodal Multi-genre Writing

EDRD 711.description: Designed to familiarize students with research findings and theories in psychology as they relate specifically to the process of learning to read. Topics will range from perception, learning theory, and personality theory to the implications of cultural differences and language factors as they affect both the child’s learning to read and the teacher’s effective facilitation of this learning.
EDRD 711.subject: EDRD
EDRD 711.title: Psychological Foundations of Reading

EDRD 714.description: An overview of major theoretical, conceptual, and historical foundations in literacy and their curricular implications. Emphasis is placed on actively analyzing current trends and related methodologies.
EDRD 714.subject: EDRD
EDRD 714.title: Critical Foundations of Literacy

EDRD 715.description: Demonstration and critical evaluation of teaching strategies and materials in reading.
EDRD 715.subject: EDRD
EDRD 715.title: Instructional Strategies for Reading

EDRD 716.description: Seminar and supervised one-on-one field experience focusing on assessing and meeting the needs of individual children as readers with emphasis on at-risk children.
EDRD 716.subject: EDRD
EDRD 716.title: Foundations of Reading Assessment

EDRD 718.description: Seminar and supervised field experience focusing on assessing and meeting the needs of small groups of children as readers.
EDRD 718.subject: EDRD
EDRD 718.title: Seminar in Classroom Reading Assessment

EDRD 719.description: Design, management, and evaluation of reading programs at the classroom, school, or district levels.
EDRD 719.subject: EDRD
EDRD 719.title: Developing and Guiding the Reading Program

EDRD 720.description: Synthesis, critique, and evaluation of current research and educational practice in language and literacy.
EDRD 720.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: EDRD 600, EDRD 715, EDRD 716, EDRD 718, and EDRD 719.
EDRD 720.subject: EDRD
EDRD 720.title: Capstone Seminar in Language and Literacy

EDRD 730.description: A survey of the strategies and materials which facilitate students’ reading and writing skill in the content areas. For P-12 reading education and content area teachers.
EDRD 730.subject: EDRD
EDRD 730.title: Teaching Reading and Writing in the Content Areas

EDRD 731.description: Overview of assessment theory and practice; the reading/writing processes and the curricular implications across content areas.
EDRD 731.subject: EDRD
EDRD 731.title: Assessment and the Foundations of Reading/Writing

EDRD 732.description: Survey of the strategies and materials which facilitate students’ reading and writing skill in the content areas.
EDRD 732.subject: EDRD
EDRD 732.title: Teaching Reading and Writing in the Content Areas

EDRD 750.description: Classroom, school, and district literacy curriculum will be explored through multicultural and global literature.
EDRD 750.subject: EDRD
EDRD 750.title: Literacy Curriculum Development

EDRD 760.description: Research and methods for literacy instruction with a focus on inquiry-based teaching and learning.
EDRD 760.subject: EDRD
EDRD 760.title: Literacy Research and Inquiry

EDRD 776.description: Coaching principles and strategies related to improvements and innovations in classrooms and in literacy instruction. Emphasizes working with teachers in classrooms to bring about educational reform and improvements in teaching and literacy instruction.
EDRD 776.subject: EDRD
EDRD 776.title: Coaching within Classrooms: Improving Teaching and Literacy Instruction

EDRD 783.description: Developing as a literacy leader within school and district contexts through: engagement in effective collaboration; design, management, and evaluation of professional learning; design, management, and evaluation of family and community outreach.
EDRD 783.subject: EDRD
EDRD 783.title: Literacy Leadership and Supervision

EDRD 794.description: An introduction to the concepts of linguistics specifically for preK-12 educators. Topics include syntax, morphology, semantics, pragmatics, and first and second language acquisition theories.
EDRD 794.subject: EDRD
EDRD 794.title: Linguistics for Classroom Teachers PreK-12

EDRD 795.description: A survey course focused on English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL), including a focus on different theoretical principles and approaches within various learning context as they concern preK-12 learners.
EDRD 795.subject: EDRD
EDRD 795.title: ESOL Principles and Strategies for PreK-12 Classrooms

EDRD 796.description: This course surveys research on the mental processes and linguistic contexts involved in reading and writing in a second language. Pedagogical implications for elementary, secondary, and postsecondary learners are discussed.
EDRD 796.subject: EDRD
EDRD 796.title: Teaching Reading and Writing to ESOL Learners: Theory and Practice

EDRD 797.description: Seminar and supervised one-on-one field experience focusing on accessing and meeting the needs of English learners including approaches to classroom-based assessments in ESL, bilingual education, and preschool-grade 12 classrooms.
EDRD 797.subject: EDRD
EDRD 797.title: Assessment for English Language Learners

EDRD 798.description: This course will engage students in the examination and creation of research and theory that support curriculum design and materials development for the ESOL classroom.
EDRD 798.subject: EDRD
EDRD 798.title: Curriculum Design and Materials Development for English Language Learners

EDRD 800.description: Impact of theories of teaching, learning, and texts on literacy instruction; social, historical, political, and cultural influences on literacy.
EDRD 800.subject: EDRD
EDRD 800.title: Literacy Education P-12

EDRD 801.description: Issues of literacy from a variety of critical stances such as democratic values, gender roles, and multiculturalism.
EDRD 801.subject: EDRD
EDRD 801.title: Critical Perspective on English/Language Arts

EDRD 802.description: Internship in diagnosis and instruction of disabled, corrective, and developing readers to include supervision of graduate students enrolled in practica in reading, parent training, and program administration. Limited to advanced graduate students. May be repeated one additional time in a different supervisory setting for a maximum of six hours.
EDRD 802.subject: EDRD
EDRD 802.title: Internship in the Supervision of Reading

EDRD 803.description: Research and theory, emphasizing the role of the reader’s response in the reading process.
EDRD 803.subject: EDRD
EDRD 803.title: Pedagogical Applications of Reader Response Theory

EDRD 805.description: Emphasis on the acquiring of background and skills necessary for instruction in and administration of college-level reading programs located in post-high school institutions (technical schools, two-year colleges, four-year colleges, and universities).
EDRD 805.subject: EDRD
EDRD 805.title: Teaching and Administrating the College Reading Program

EDRD 806.description: Refining of counseling, evaluation, research, instructional, and administrative skills needed by college reading personnel. Practical application of the background and skills taught in EDRD 805 .
EDRD 806.subject: EDRD
EDRD 806.title: Practicum in Teaching and Administering the College Reading Program

EDRD 811.description: Perspectives from psychology and sociocultural theory as they relate to literacy learning and research in literacy learning.
EDRD 811.subject: EDRD
EDRD 811.title: Cultural Perspective on Psychological and Social Foundations of Literacy Learning

EDRD 815.description: A review and critique of qualitative perspectives on language and literacy research.
EDRD 815.subject: EDRD
EDRD 815.title: Critique of Qualitative Research in Language and Literacy Education

EDRD 824.description: Intensive study of a designated topic influencing theory and/or practice in language and literacy education.
EDRD 824.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Admission to a doctoral program in education or related field.
EDRD 824.subject: EDRD
EDRD 824.title: Seminar in Language and Literacy Education

EDRD 840.description: Peircean semiotics and the implications of such for language and literacy education.
EDRD 840.subject: EDRD
EDRD 840.title: Semiotics, Reading, Literacy and Learning

EDRD 842.description: An exploration of the reading process and how readers construct meaning by relating their sociopsycholinguistic backgrounds to discourse, including analysis of reading miscues at several linguistic levels, an examination of assessment and instructional tools, and developing a comprehension centered reading program.
EDRD 842.subject: EDRD
EDRD 842.title: Windows into the Reading Process

EDRD 844.description: Historical and contemporary language issues in society, language diversity and marginalization, theoretical frameworks and findings.
EDRD 844.subject: EDRD
EDRD 844.title: Language Acquisition in Society

EDRD 845.description: Conceptual frameworks, findings, and connections among current and classic studies in emergent literacy; implications for further research.
EDRD 845.subject: EDRD
EDRD 845.title: Advanced Study of Emergent Literacy

EDRD 848.description: Current theories of gender identity in relationship to literacy education.
EDRD 848.subject: EDRD
EDRD 848.title: Feminist Investigation in Literacy Education

EDRD 850.description: Placement in an agency or higher education setting to gain supervised experience in literacy program planning and/or research. May be repeated once for a total of 6 hours.
EDRD 850.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 6 hours of required language and literacy courses in the language and literacy PhD program.
EDRD 850.subject: EDRD
EDRD 850.title: Internship in Language and Literacy Education
